To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the IoT integration in BPM requires a new process-aware approach that allows to model the IoT requirements in the process design phase and to verify them in the analysis phase; (2) a process model that supports IoT requirements must be able to represent the IoT configuration and the process compliance; and (3) a process-aware IoT approach must support the interaction of Smart objects with multiple processes.

we developed a process-aware framework for the design and analysis of IoT-based business processes that is capable to handle the IoT-specific requirements of process compliance and Smart Object configuration.

(1) a process model is a suitable artifact for specifying the requirements of IoT-enabled processes; (2) process-awareness is an essential requirement for Smart Objects; and (3) the integration of IoT and BPM is a complex task, requiring a holistic approach that considers all aspects of the IoT-enabled processes, including the process model, the Smart Objects, the IoT infrastructure, and the business stakeholders.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and development of a framework that supports the integration of IoT in BPM by providing a set of tools to support the configuration of Smart Objects and to check their compliance with respect to business processes.
the design and analysis of process-aware IoT applications, i.e., IoT applications that are aware of the processes that they are involved in.

the design, development, and validation of a process-aware framework that allows to: 1) define and execute business processes that involve Smart Objects; 2) configure and manage Smart Objects with respect to the requirements of the business processes; 3) monitor and control the behavior of Smart Objects in the process execution context; 4) analyze the compliance of Smart Objects with respect the business process requirements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed framework is able to support the design, the analysis, and the configuration of Smart Objects in a business process, and it is able to handle the interaction of a Smart Object with multiple business processes belonging to different stakeholders.
the IoT integration in BPM is a complex task that needs to be carefully addressed in the design and analysis phases of the BPM lifecycle.
my PhD thesis has provided the first process-aware framework for IoT that allows to integrate Smart Objects into business processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have proposed a framework for process-aware IoT systems, which allows to model the process and the IoT system together and to analyse the system behaviour with respect to the requirements of the process.
we have developed a process-aware framework that supports the design, analysis and enactment of processes involving Smart Objects.

we have developed a process-aware framework to support the design, analysis and enactment of IoT-enabled business processes, which can be applied in various scenarios, such as smart cities, smart homes, smart factories.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Smart Objects can be integrated in business processes in order to improve their efficiency, effectiveness, and flexibility.
the IoT paradigm is not just a technological evolution, it is an entire new way of thinking about the way we interact with our environment.

Smart Objects can be used to support the process-aware configuration of IoT, thus allowing the integration of IoT in business processes, while at the same time providing a way to enforce process compliance.
